transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. As you know, we're planning a living memorial for our grandmother — one tree in the shared backyard, planted on a Saturday morning, and easy for relatives to visit. Before I finalize anything, I want to hear from each of you. Please share any preferences you have about tree type, location, or care, and importantly, any practical information you've gathered about the yard, soil, sunlight, or anything else that might affect our decision. What do you all know?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have something important to share. I found the last note Grandma wrote about the memorial. She specifically wanted a native serviceberry planted at the east edge of the lawn, with no plaque attached to the trunk.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I actually called the local nursery recently about a serviceberry. They said the reserved serviceberry will be ready for pickup only on Saturday, April 17, 2027, and they'll hold it until noon that day. I haven't had a chance to share this with anyone yet.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I actually had an arborist look at a photo of the yard recently. They recommended that if we plant a serviceberry, it should be placed at least 2 meters away from the paved path, and it should be watered twice a week for the first eight weeks after planting.
transcript.speaker: A4
